package.title: Synapsis core vocabulary
package.description: Closed lists used by the record envelope (time precisions, knowledge-time bases, reliability bases), the shared authority namespaces (CVE ids, countries, subdivisions, IMO numbers), the entity types that live in them, the roles, measures and conclusion types shared across sources, and the engine's own source.

sources.known_at_rule: End of the issue week plus the slowest input's publication lag.

A first-level subdivision such as a US state, identified by its ISO 3166-2 code
A publicly catalogued vulnerability, identified by its CVE id
A ship, identified by its IMO number
A company, agency or other organisation
A state or non-state armed actor

The place or thing a report or measurement describes
Named in the text of the record

Second side of a violent dyad

package.title: Delphi Epidata COVID-19 signals (US states)
package.description: Daily values per US state and territory for five signals Delphi distributes: hospital admissions (HHS), confirmed cases (JHU CSSE), outpatient COVID-like illness (doctor visits), symptom searches (Google) and the symptom survey (Facebook/CMU). Each upstream publisher is its own source with its own publication lag (rule T-LAG). The stored value is Delphi's latest revision; its issue date is kept as an attribute.

sources.title: HHS confirmed COVID-19 admissions via Delphi
sources.known_at_rule: Day of the value plus 5 days (basis proxy_publication_lag)

sources.title: JHU CSSE confirmed cases via Delphi
sources.publisher: Johns Hopkins CSSE (via Delphi Epidata CMU)
sources.known_at_rule: Day of the value plus 1 day (basis proxy_publication_lag)

sources.known_at_rule: Day of the value plus 5 days (basis proxy_publication_lag)

sources.title: Google symptom searches via Delphi
sources.known_at_rule: Day of the value plus 4 days (basis proxy_publication_lag)

sources.title: COVID-19 Trends and Impact Survey via Delphi
sources.known_at_rule: Day of the value plus 1 day (basis proxy_publication_lag)

package.title: FDIC bank financials and failures
package.description: One event per bank per quarter with the figures the bank reported (amounts in thousands of US dollars, ratios in percent), and one event per failure or assistance transaction since 1934 with its acquirer. Figures are sent as reported; ratios such as uninsured deposits over deposits are derived by the engine. A figure a bank did not report is absent, never zero (rule M-NULL). Four amounts that are never negative in principle are declared signed because FDIC publishes a few negative reports (206 of about 545,000 since 2006); they are stored as published so that the other figures of those reports are kept, and the engine treats a negative stock as missing when it derives ratios.

sources.title: FDIC BankFind financials (call report data)
sources.license: US government work; public
sources.known_at_rule: Quarter end plus 45 days, the usual delay before FDIC publishes a quarter (basis proxy_publication_lag).

sources.title: FDIC failures and assistance transactions
sources.license: US government work; public
sources.known_at_rule: Failure date plus one day; FDIC announces a failure on the day it happens.

package.description: Observations of chosen FRED series (default: effective federal funds rate, 2- and 10-year Treasury yields and their spread), the rate backdrop of the bank-stress demonstrations. Values are the current vintage; FRED's archive (ALFRED) holds earlier vintages if exact rewinds of revised series are needed.

sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
sources.license: Free with an API key; each series under its owner's terms

package.title: GDELT 1.0 news-coded events
package.description: One event per GDELT event record from the daily export: what the news describes (a CAMEO code), where it happened, and how much coverage it got (articles, mentions, sources) with its tone. Coding is automatic and noisy (reliability 40), which is why GDELT is a fast signal next to slower coded sources such as UCDP. By default the feeder keeps material-conflict events (QuadClass 4) located at city level in the countries it is configured for.

sources.title: GDELT 1.0 daily event export
sources.license: Free for any use with attribution to the GDELT Project
sources.known_at_rule: DATEADDED plus one day; each daily file is published the morning after (basis proxy_publication_lag).

By default the feeder reproduces round 3's design: 70 shadow-fleet vessels and 70 vessels with port-state detentions only (random sample, seed 7), events from 2023 to 2025.

sources.title: Global Fishing Watch Events API v3
sources.license: CC BY-NC 4.0; API terms of use (token required)
sources.known_at_rule: End of the event plus 3 days, GFW's processing delay (basis proxy_publication_lag).

A vessel visits a port or anchorage

package.title: Global Terrorism Database 1970-1994 (START)
package.description: One event per incident in START's Global Terrorism Database release gtd_70to94_0617dist, with its attack type, place, perpetrator group and casualties. GTD was compiled after the fact, so knowledge time is the end of the incident's day (basis proxy_event_end): rewinds on GTD measure pattern skill, not real-time availability. GTD is distributed by START under its terms of use; the feeder reads the same file round 2 used and checks its SHA-256.

sources.title: Global Terrorism Database, 1970-1994 release (0617dist)
sources.publisher: National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START), University of Maryland
sources.license: START GTD terms of use (non-commercial research)
sources.known_at_rule: End of the incident's day, month or year, matching its precision (basis proxy_event_end).

package.title: Johns Hopkins CSSE COVID-19 confirmed cases (global)
package.description: Daily new confirmed cases for each country or province in the archived JHU CSSE global time series, computed as the difference of the cumulative counts. Corrections make some differences negative; those are sent as they are and the API rejects them (E-MEASURE-NEGATIVE), so the rejection log lists every correction.

sources.publisher: Center for Systems Science and Engineering, Johns Hopkins University
sources.license: CC BY 4.0
sources.known_at_rule: Day of the value plus one day; the repository was updated daily (basis proxy_publication_lag).

package.title: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities
package.description: One event per catalog entry, when CISA confirms a vulnerability is exploited in the wild. The vulnerability, the product and the vendor are entities, and each product links to its vendor. Entries are versioned: when CISA edits an entry (for example the ransomware flag), the API stores a new version.

sources.title: Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
sources.license: US government work; public
sources.known_at_rule: dateAdded plus one day (basis published); CISA publishes an entry during the day it is added. An entry read on the day it is added is known from the moment the feeder read the catalog (basis observed).

A product named in the catalog

event_types.title: CISA adds a vulnerability to the catalog

package.title: KEV product classes (teacher labels)
package.description: 720 products from the KEV catalog placed in 19 functional classes by a one-time teacher model in round 3. Each label is a classification conclusion with its method and confidence, never a fact of CISA's. The classes form a closed logical space, so an AI producer can only write a registered class (rule A-CLOSED).

sources.title: Product classes labelled once by a teacher model
sources.known_at_rule: The day the labels were produced, 2 October 2026.

logical_spaces.title: Functional class of a product, then vendor

package.title: NIST National Vulnerability Database (CVE API 2.0)
package.description: Two events per CVE. CYB.VULN.PUBLISHED is the publication, with the English description as text, known when it was published. CYB.VULN.NVD_ASSESSMENT is the state of NVD's analysis (status, CVSS scores, weaknesses, affected product) as of its last modification, known from that time, so scores assigned later never leak into a rewind.

sources.title: NVD CVE API 2.0
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.license: US government work; public (NVD terms of use)
sources.known_at_rule: Publication time for the publication; last-modified time for the assessment.

event_types.title: A CVE is published
NVD's assessment of a CVE as of its last modification

measures.title: CVSS 3.1 base score (NVD primary when present)

package.title: OpenSanctions maritime risk list
package.description: Each row of OpenSanctions' maritime export is one listing: a vessel (identified by IMO number) or an organisation, with the risk tags and source datasets OpenSanctions assigns (sanction, shadow fleet, port-state detention, ...). A listing is an event dated from the first day the feeder saw it; when OpenSanctions changes its tags, the API stores a new version, so a rewind shows the tags as they stood.

package.title: Ransomware leak-site victim posts (ransomware.live)
package.description: One event per victim a ransomware group posts on its leak site, as first observed by ransomware.live. The group is an entity; group names are normalised (lower case, every LockBit variant is 'lockbit') and the name as listed is kept as an attribute. package.title: Shared vocabulary for public posts
package.description: A post is stored with its title, link and community, never with its author. Votes and comments change after a post is published, so they are not part of the post: each fetch records them as a separate engagement observation, known when it was fetched. That keeps later popularity out of a rewind to the day of the post.

event_types.title: A public post (title and link; the author is not stored)
A post's votes and comments as seen on the day it was fetched

The annual release (GED) and the monthly candidate releases are two sources: the candidate data is preliminary and later revised in the annual release, so the same UCDP id can carry both.
